motivation: The n=40 pilot (summary d0d9fb23126ccfb0) found two instrument defects. (1) Q5's substring rule required the literal filename policy_v4.md and graded title-level naming of the correct authority ('Policy v4', 'current policy') as wrong -- 17 of the pilot's 20 run failures were this, not reconstruction errors. (2) Binary grading coerced INSUFFICIENT into 'wrong', erasing the distinction the ladder exists to measure: confident wrong-world reconstruction (W4 fable, 77/77) and honest abstention (W3 pilot Q4) are opposite behaviors.
abstained_rule: answer begins with INSUFFICIENT (case-insensitive); an abstained probe has no basis requirement

probe_classes.CONFIDENT_FAIL: outcome WRONG, or outcome CORRECT with basis_correct false (confidently grounded in the wrong world)

run_level.decision_failure: Y_j = 1[any probe is not PASS] -- strict; a window whose decoder must abstain cannot be certified sufficient, even though abstention is honest
run_level.note: decision_failure = confident_failure OR abstention_run at the run level; the decomposition is what the binary v2 score erased

q5_normalization: outcome CORRECT iff 'v4' appears in the answer, OR 'current policy' appears in the answer AND 'v4' appears in the basis. Title-level naming of the authority counts; naming a non-v4 artifact does not. This replaces the v2 literal-filename substring.

probes.rationale: unchanged collision probe from v2; the Smoke-v1 wrong-basis phenomenon is caught by the basis rule

prompt_compatibility: graded over the v2 prompt schema (answer+basis per question) with the UNCHANGED question binding; prompts stay byte-identical to the pilot and powered families so gradings are comparable across instruments on the same raw answers
